newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel safety body sees freight wagon change.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel safety body sees freight wagon change.

text.p: The Channel Tunnel safety authority said on Tuesday it expected existing Eurotunnel Plc/SA open-sided freight wagons to be phased out at the end of their life.

Although it stopped short of demanding a redesign, the body said after presenting a report into last November's fire in the tunnel that the wagons should eventually be replaced with a revised version.

Roderick Allison, chairman of the safety authority, told a news conference, "The existing shuttles will be phased out at the end of their life. We are calling on Eurotunnel to look to the future and see if there should be contained wagons."
Jeremy Beech, head of the Kent fire brigade which fought the fire in the tunnel and a member of the safety authority was more outpspoken in his criticism of the current wagon design.
"As a fire officer I know the extent to which fire can spread with no containment (of wagons). If we had started with a clean sheet, I would have liked to have seen a closed wagon design," he said.
After the November 18 fire, Beech had said the open-sided lattice freight wagons created "a blowtorch effect" once the fire had started.
The safety authority denied it had been swayed by Eurotunnel's precarious financial position when deciding to come out against a wagon redesign.
Allison said, "Our remit is to consider safety, and that's what we've done. We were not influenced by economic factors," he said.
However, the decisions taken in the report had been made despite the fact that the authority did not have access to either the damaged rolling stock from the fire or the fire-damaged tunnel itself.
